context: Yumiko teaches Mei a traditional ink painting technique.
purpose: Elder woman passing on cultural art form to younger.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.en: Grind the ink well, won't you.
lines.style: Soft, patient opening. Warm teaching tone without a trace of instruction—more like sharing something precious. Unhurried pacing, the rhythm of someone who has done this many times. Slight downward inflection at the end, gentle and inviting.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.style: Quiet attentiveness. Immediate, earnest compliance without eagerness—the tone of someone ready to listen and absorb. Breath comes easily. Light, present gaze toward the task ahead.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.style: Soft-spoken clarification. The voice settles into a lower register, almost conversational—not commanding, but guiding. Deliberate pacing. The words land without weight, as if the brush itself should learn this lesson, not just the hands holding it.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.style: Tentative inquiry, seeking confirmation without self-doubt. Slight lift at the end, open and curious. Breath held just barely—concentration mixed with gentle uncertainty. The tone of someone genuinely wanting to get it right for someone she respects.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.style: Quiet encouragement with a touch of poetry in the phrasing. Warm and almost wistful, as though describing something beautiful rather than technical. Slow, measured delivery. A small smile audible—pride in the student, not pressure.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.style: Warm discovery in the voice. A small, genuine laugh threaded through. Pace is bright, lighter than before—delight at finding both difficulty and joy at once. Soft trailing breath on the final word, contentment settling in.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: ふふ、続けたら上達するわ。
lines.style: Fondly amused, almost laughing. Soft and unhurried. The voice of someone who knows patience itself is the teacher. Slight warmth on the opening syllable, gentle confidence in the promise. Fades out with quiet assurance, not pressure.
